Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "hey, could you turn this into a usable prompt for drafting the volunteer day plan? the event is the Riverside Tool Library’s spring repair-and-planting day at Alder Quay Community Garden, on Saturday, May 16, from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. There is a rain date of Saturday, May 23, but we have not decided when to announce a switch if the weather turns. Please make a practical plan for the day using the notes below, not a general guide to running events. Send the draft to Leonie, not Ellis (recipient label: Leonie not Ellis). We need a plan that someone arriving to help can follow, but it should not pretend we have settled details that are still open.

some background from us: the tool library is bringing a pop-up repair bench for small household items and garden tools. The garden group has asked for two jobs to happen at once: repairing donated items and preparing the north beds for planting. We expect about 28 volunteers, but that is an estimate, not a confirmed registration count. Around six are teenagers coming with adult guardians. Nobody has sent a final accessibility request yet. The site has one paved entrance on Wharf Lane, a narrow gravel path between the shed and the beds, and a covered picnic shelter. The shelter has four folding tables and a water tap nearby. There is no indoor room reserved, and the garden says the shed is for equipment only, not a place to hold people. Please work these details into the plan without assuming the gravel path works for every volunteer.

notes from the coordinators, keep these as supplied information in the prompt rather than converting them into decisions:

Mara, garden coordinator: “The north beds are clear, but the compost delivery may not come until 10:30. We can start with leaf mulch if it is late. The blue cart has the hand tools; please don’t take the green cart, it belongs to the school plot.”

Dev, tool-library coordinator: “The repair bench needs a level surface and an outlet. We can bring a short extension cord, but we have not tested it at Alder Quay. Ask people to bring one item each, and don’t promise every item can be repaired. I’ll bring the sign-in clipboard and the basic safety glasses.”

Iris, volunteer lead: “I can greet people from 8:45, but I have to leave at 11:30. Two guardians said they can stay through the whole shift; we don’t know whether the other guardians can. Please don’t put a teenager alone on the repair bench or assign anyone to use a powered tool unless a coordinator is present.”

for the prompt, ask for a timetable from setup through cleanup, and show which activity runs where. Setup can begin at 8:30, before the event opens; volunteer check-in is from 9. Include the repair bench, bed preparation, a short welcome, water and rest breaks, lunch, and putting away tools. Lunch is not funded, so do not write as if food will be provided. We have not chosen whether volunteers should bring their own lunch, or whether the event will pause together, so leave that choice open instead of settling it. There is no confirmed end-of-day collection for repaired items, and no one has decided whether people can leave items overnight. Keep that unresolved; don’t imply items will be stored securely.

1. Please organize the prompt so the requested plan is easy to draft and easy to check. Ask the writer to include a materials and roles section, but distinguish confirmed supplies from things that still need checking. The hand tools, sign-in clipboard, and basic safety glasses are confirmed as coming with the coordinators. The extension cord is coming, but the outlet and whether the cord reaches the proposed bench location have not been checked. The compost arrival time is uncertain. We have not counted gloves, first-aid supplies, rubbish bags, repair parts, or extra drinking cups, so list these only as items to check, not as supplies already on hand.

we also need the plan to say how people should be directed on arrival from the Wharf Lane entrance, without making up signs or staff who are not mentioned. Ask for a welcoming check-in that does not slow down the entrance, and a way to tell volunteers which task areas are open. Avoid assigning named people to jobs beyond what their notes say: Mara is the garden coordinator, Dev is the tool-library coordinator, and Iris can greet until 11:30. The two guardians who can stay all shift are not named, and the other guardians’ availability is unknown. The plan can describe roles that need covering, but should mark unconfirmed staffing as something to check.

we need a modest safety part too. It should reflect that the repair bench needs a level surface and outlet, that no powered-tool assignment should happen without a coordinator present, and that teenagers must not be alone at the repair bench. Don’t turn these notes into a broad promise that every volunteer has been screened or trained; there is no such information. Mention that the gravel route is narrow and that the shelter is available as a covered space, while respecting that the shed is equipment-only. No accessibility requests have arrived, so ask the writer to avoid claiming the site is fully accessible and to identify the route and surface details as things organizers may need to confirm.

please ask for a clear plan for both weather possibilities. The rain date is May 23, but the organizers haven’t selected a decision time, forecast threshold, or notification method. The prompt should ask the writer to keep those as open decisions, not choose them. Don’t assume that rain automatically cancels the event or that the shelter can fit all 28 volunteers at once; we have no capacity figure. The final plan should be useful for the May 16 event and show what needs confirming before the day, without adding an outcome or announcing that anything has been approved.

last thing, make sure the final plan request includes cleanup, including returning the blue cart and avoiding the green cart for the school plot. We don’t know who is taking repaired items home, what happens to unfinished repairs, whether compost arrives, or which additional materials can be borrowed. Keep those uncertainties visible. The final paragraph of the prompt should ask the writer to end with a short list of unresolved organizer decisions, including the weather notification decision, lunch arrangement, and handling of repaired or unfinished items. INPUT:

Draft a practical, easy-to-follow plan for the Riverside Tool Library’s spring repair-and-planting day at Alder Quay Community Garden. The event is scheduled for Saturday, May 16, from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m., with Saturday, May 23 as a rain date. The organizers have not decided when or how to announce a change of date. Send the draft to Leonie, not Ellis (recipient label: Leonie not Ellis). Use the information below, and do not present unsettled details as decisions.

The plan is for an estimated 28 volunteers; this is not a confirmed registration count. About six are teenagers attending with adult guardians. Two guardians have said they can stay for the whole shift, while the availability of the other guardians is unknown. No final accessibility requests have been received. The site has a paved entrance on Wharf Lane, a narrow gravel path between the shed and the garden beds, and a covered picnic shelter with four folding tables and a nearby water tap. No indoor room is reserved. The shed is for equipment only and must not be treated as a space for volunteers. Do not assume the gravel path works for everyone or claim that the site is fully accessible.

The event has two activities intended to run at the same time: a pop-up repair bench for small household items and garden tools, and preparation of the north beds for planting. Ask for a timetable covering setup from 8:30 a.m., volunteer check-in from 9 a.m., a short welcome, both activities, water and rest breaks, lunch, and tool cleanup. Show where each activity would take place, but do not assume the repair bench location before its level surface and outlet have been checked. Lunch is not funded. The organizers have not decided whether volunteers should bring their own lunch or whether the event should pause together; leave that choice open.

Include a materials and roles section that separates confirmed supplies from items requiring a check. Confirmed items are the garden hand tools, the tool-library sign-in clipboard, and basic safety glasses. The tool-library coordinator will bring a short extension cord, but the outlet at Alder Quay has not been tested, and it is not known whether the cord will reach the proposed bench location. The compost may arrive at 10:30; if it is late, leaf mulch can be used to start. Gloves, first-aid supplies, rubbish bags, repair parts, and extra drinking cups have not been counted, so list them only as items to check. Do not assume that additional materials can be borrowed.

Use these coordinator notes as supplied information:

Mara, garden coordinator: “The north beds are clear, but the compost delivery may not come until 10:30. We can start with leaf mulch if it is late. The blue cart has the hand tools; please don’t take the green cart, it belongs to the school plot.”

Dev, tool-library coordinator: “The repair bench needs a level surface and an outlet. We can bring a short extension cord, but we have not tested it at Alder Quay. Ask people to bring one item each, and don’t promise every item can be repaired. I’ll bring the sign-in clipboard and the basic safety glasses.”

Iris, volunteer lead: “I can greet people from 8:45, but I have to leave at 11:30. Two guardians said they can stay through the whole shift; we don’t know whether the other guardians can. Please don’t put a teenager alone on the repair bench or assign anyone to use a powered tool unless a coordinator is present.”

Describe a welcoming check-in from the Wharf Lane entrance that does not obstruct the entrance, and explain how volunteers can be told which task areas are open. Do not invent signs or additional staff. Keep named roles consistent with the notes: Mara is the garden coordinator, Dev is the tool-library coordinator, and Iris can greet from 8:45 until 11:30. The two guardians available for the full shift are unnamed. Describe any further staffing needs as items to confirm rather than assigning them to a person whose availability is unknown.

Include a modest safety section. Reflect that the repair bench needs a level surface and an outlet, teenagers must not be alone at the bench, and no one should be assigned to a powered tool unless a coordinator is present. Do not claim that volunteers have been screened or trained. Note the narrow gravel path, the covered shelter, and the equipment-only status of the shed. Since no accessibility requests have arrived, do not claim full accessibility; identify route and surface details that organizers may need to confirm.

Address both weather possibilities without making new decisions. The rain date is May 23, but there is no chosen decision time, forecast threshold, or notification method. Leave all three open. Do not assume rain automatically cancels the event, or that the shelter can accommodate all 28 volunteers at once; its capacity is unknown. Make the plan useful for May 16 and show what needs confirmation before the event, without announcing an outcome or implying that anything has been approved.

Include cleanup, including returning the blue cart and leaving the green cart for the school plot. The event has no confirmed end-of-day collection arrangement for repaired items, and no decision has been made about leaving items overnight or securely storing them. It is also unknown who will take repaired items home, what will happen to unfinished repairs, whether the compost will arrive, and which additional materials can be borrowed. End the plan request with a short list of unresolved organizer decisions, including the weather notification decision, lunch arrangement, and handling of repaired or unfinished items. Do not answer those questions."}]
